answers.solution:
Solution written to `/home/kara/SOLUTION-gitreins-wrong-interpreter.md`.

I reproduced the root-cause mechanism locally with the available interpreters (no GitReins/terminal-jail repo present in this sandbox):

- **Broken PATH** (tool venv first, as the docs taught): `pytest` resolves to the tool venv's older Python → `ModuleNotFoundError` on a version-gated stdlib import → `1 error during collection`.
- **Fixed PATH** (repo `.venv/bin` first): bare `pytest` resolves to the repo interpreter → passes.
- **Config pin** (`.venv/bin/python -m pytest`) with the *same broken PATH*: passes, proving the pin removes PATH dependence.

The document contains:

1. **Title/symptom** — false tests-lane RED, `1 error in collection`, `tomllib` on Python 3.10.20.
2. **Root cause** — the PATH entry making `gitreins` resolvable also selects the GitReins venv's 3.10 `pytest`, so the lane graded the interpreter instead of the code; plus the AGENTS.md doc propagation trap.
3. **Distinguishing triage table** — collection error vs real failure, header Python vs repo Python, version-gated stdlib module, same-commit cross-check.
4. **Exact fix** — `.gitreins/config.yaml` `guards.test_command: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -x --tb=short` (durable fix), and the corrected AGENTS.md PATH order `$HOME/go/bin:<repo>/.venv/bin:<gitreins-venv>/bin:$PATH` with the one-line "why".
5. **Verification** — before/after guard logs, plus a self-contained local reproduction (Cases A/B/C) using two venvs and a version-gated stdlib import.
6. **Transferable rule** — gates must pin the interpreter, not inherit it from PATH.

signatures.description:
SYMPTOM (GitReins harness): `gitreins guard --full` reported
`Tier 1 Guards: FAIL  ✗ tests (full) — 1 error in 0.25s` on a tree whose suite is
green (671 passed / 5 skipped) when run with the documented invocation
`PATH="$HOME/go/bin:$HOME/gitreins-poc/.venv/bin:$PATH" gitreins guard`. The guard
log showed:

    collected 548 items / 1 error
    ERROR collecting plugin/test_packaging.py
    plugin/test_packaging.py:27: import tomllib
    E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tomllib'
    platform linux -- Python 3.10.20, pytest-9.1.1

ROOT CAUSE: the GitReins CLI lives in its own venv, and that venv is Python 3.10
and ships its own `pytest`. Putting it first on PATH (the standard way to make
`gitreins` resolvable) also makes `pytest` resolve to the 3.10 interpreter, so the
guard's tests lane collects the whole tree under 3.10 even though the repository
requires 3.11+ (`tomllib` is stdlib from 3.11). The gate is failing on the
INTERPRETER, not on the code — and it fails identically on trees whose suite would
pass, i.e. it is a false RED that trains operators to ignore the tests lane.

DIAGNOSIS THAT DISTINGUISHES IT FROM A REAL TEST FAILURE:
- the failure is a COLLECTION error (`1 error`, not `N failed`), reported before any
  test ran;
- the pytest header names a different Python than the repo venv (`Python 3.10.20`
  while `.venv/bin/python -V` says 3.11.15);
- the missing module is a STDLIB module whose availability is version-gated
  (`tomllib` 3.11+, `except*`/`Self`/`StrEnum` are the same class);
- the same commit passes when the tests lane runs under the repo interpreter.

FIXES (either is sufficient; both together is what we landed):
1. Pin the tests lane to the repo interpreter in `.gitreins/config.yaml`:
   `guards.test_command: .venv/bin/python -m pytest -x --tb=short`. This makes the
   lane independent of PATH ordering, which is the durable fix — any other tool
   resolved from PATH (ruff, gitleaks) can still come from wherever it comes from.
2. Document a PATH order that works: `PATH="$HOME/go/bin:<repo>/.venv/bin:<gitreins-venv>/bin:$PATH"` —
   the repo venv must PRECEDE the GitReins venv, and `gitreins` itself still resolves
   from the later entry. A one-line "why" beside it saves the next reader 30 minutes.

VERIFICATION (both directions, same host, same commit):
- BEFORE: guard log guard-20260919T005837, `Tier 1 Guards: FAIL`, tests lane
  `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tomllib'`, Python 3.10.20.
- AFTER the config pin, re-running the guard with the OLD (broken) PATH:
  `Tier 1 Guards: PASS  (test mode: full, whole tree)` — secrets/lint/tests/static
  all green, guard log guard-20260919T012604.

RELATED TRAP: if the repo's own docs teach the broken PATH (an AGENTS.md line), the
false RED reproduces for every agent that follows the docs, and it reads as "the
repo's tests are broken" in every sync/audit report. Both halves have to move: fix
the config AND the documented command.

TRANSFERABLE RULE: a quality gate that shells out to a language toolchain must pin
the INTERPRETER, not inherit it from PATH. When a CLI tool ships its own venv, the
PATH that makes the tool resolvable is exactly the PATH that silently changes which
runtime grades your code.
